newsitem.title: FINLAND: July GDP shows Finnish growth robust -economists.
newsitem.headline: July GDP shows Finnish growth robust -economists.

text.p: Finnish July GDP growth at nearly four percent showed the economy had embarked onto the forecast path of accelerating growth, economists said on Friday.
"It strengthens the impression that the mini-recession has been left behind," said chief economist Risto Murto at brokerage Selin Finance.
"It tells you that there is a solid basis for recently upgraded more optimistic growth forecasts," he said.
Statistics Finland (SF) reported a pick-up in gross domestic product growth to 3.9 percent year-on-year in July against 2.4 percent in June, and the highest any month since August 1995.
The July growth figure was "just the kind needed" for full-year 1996 GDP growth of 2.5 percent as forecast by the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA), said ETLA researcher Hannu Kaseva.
But Postipankki economist Lauri Uotila was slightly more cautious. "It is a change in a good direction, but not sufficient evidence that the pace of growth actually has picked up," he said.
All three economists pointed out that the July GDP figure was boosted by an exceptionally big increase, five percent, in industrial production -- mainly due to fewer holidays in July.
The timing of orders won by the metal, engineering and electrotechnical industry -- now the chief engine of export growth -- had required more work in July this year, they said.
"The emphasis was now on the metal industry," ETLA's Kaseva said. "The timing of summer holidays was slightly different this year than last," he added.
Uotila at Postipankki said this meant that holidays may have focused more on August; so the growth rate that month may turn out clearly poorer than the July figure.
SF is due to release August industrial production data on October 15.
Despite the clear growth in July industrial production, it would be incorrect to assume this equalled a massive increase in actual output, Uotila said.
Although the timing of holidays was different, July was still Finland's main holiday month: "the weight of July is less than one-twelfth of full-year production," he said.
GDP was also boosted by trade and commerce output, which increased 5.5 percent in July, Statistics Finland reported.
Economists said sales of consumer electronics had posted very big increases because of the Olympic summer games in Atlanta, which started late in July.
The economists agreed that there was no danger of inflation even if growth continued strong during the end of this year and throughout 1997.
"In 1996 and 1997 it is difficult to see any significant inflation pressures," said Murto at Selin.

"There is no danger of inflation for at least one and a half years," ETLA's Kaseva said, adding there was plenty of room for the Bank of Finland to further trim its tender rate, currently at 3.10 percent.
In August, Finnish CPI rose 0.4 percent year-on-year.
--Peter Starck, Helsinki Newsroom +358 - 0 - 680 50 245
